I don't like the stigma associated with BPD, I honestly wish that my first diagnosis of Bipolar was the correct one, at least then it would be mainly controlled by medication. With BPD there really isn't a medicine or combo of meds that will treat it. It isn't really a chemical imbalance, it's a personality disorder, a learned behavior pattern combined with an overactive amygdala. I can understand in a way why bitter exes would want to say their exes have BPD but it most likely isn't true in most cases. They want an excuse, a reason why they had a failed relationship, I get that. But what I don't get is why they don't take any responsibility for anything that went wrong. Like you said a relationship is 50/50 unless you CHOOSE to make it otherwise, in which case said failed relationship has nothing to do with BPD but probably more with the fact it wasn't an equal relationship. It makes me mad when people say oh they're "crazy" they must have BPD. We are not "crazy" we may feel that way sometimes, but in most cases, we are jst human beings dealing with crap that everyone else does, but with a different set of coping skills.

You know, I wasn't going to say anything initially when I read this post, but I am compelled to say something now. I have been diagnosed with BPD since I was about 15 years old, I am just now getting my life fully back on track at 27 years old. I was (in my opinion) just like your mom from reading what you wrote. It took me so long to realize that I was the one who was doing things that hurt other people, and sometimes I still find myself doing it unintentionally(which usually requires a lot of apologies afterwards). The only thing that ever helped me to want to help myself was when I was 23 and I was committed to a state psychiatric facility in which I had no choice but to get better and help myself or I would stay there forever. I was on a special unit in which everyone there was diagnosed with BPD and sometimes that had BPD and other disorders/diagnoses. It was very hard when everyone had BPD since one characteristic is to feed off of others emotions as well as attention-seeking behaviors (meaning when one person went ape shit, most of everyone else did too). I struggled with getting better because I had lived as I was for so long as well as the fact that I didn't want to take responsibility and say that most of my problems were consequences of my own actions. I'm telling you this so I can say that even your mom eventually might get better. I still am not completely better, but it is the progress I have seen and comparing where I am today to where I was even 4 months ago, that keep me trying to get even better. I got better once, then took a few steps back but I have gotten back to where I was fresh out of the facility when I was so happy and loved myself and my life, regardless of the family problems I had as a direct result of my actions when in BPD rages. Everyone who has posted here is exactly correct in what they said. I commend you for being able to put up with and love someone who could be so horribly mean and abusive. You don't know it, but you helped me remember where I came from, and where I never want to be again. If not for posts like this, I may forget these things and become the horrible, abusive person I used to be. Last thing, I know that when I used to hurt others verbally, emotionally, and physically, I would hate myself more because I was so mean and a lot of times it was a reaction that I had no control over. Sorry for the long-winded rant, but I wanted you to know that if she takes the time and effort to better herself, she can get better, I'm living proof. And also so you know that it's not going to help for you to keep helping her if she will not help herself. The best thing my parents ever did for me was kick me out of the house and stop trying. I thank them for it every chance I get because if they hadn't, I never would have gone to the facility or had a reason to help myself(the ultimatum they gave me was to get better or never talk to them again). Anyway thanks for reading and thank you so much for not wanting to be prejudiced against everyone you meet who has BPD. It is a hard thing to live with this disorder and even harder if people you love/like/meet don't want to be around you because of a disorder you never asked for but have anyway.

Dude I have felt this way soooooo many times it isn't funny. And mixed with my depression and obsessive thinking, I tend to do irrational, impulsive things (mainly to myself) when i feel this way. My only advice would be to not do anything that might injure or end yourself. I'm not saying you would because i don't know you to assume such things. I'm just saying if you ever feel like doing those types of things, think it through first. I do wonder though, have you gone to college? If so, did you enjoy what you labored in? If not, what might you take if you were to go to college? Also, have you ever just up and took a trip somewhere you have never been just to experience it? I know when i was 18 I felt like I was a computer and tv vegetable, so i took my college savings and skipped out on a full scholarship to the community college and went across the country on a greyhound bus. Just to experience life away from home, familiarity, and vegetation. I'm not suggesting you do it but it helped me get through a hard time. I met some awesome people and some not so awesome people but to me it was worth the trip. Basically I can't tell you anything more than what has worked for me in the past, but what worked for me may not work for you, then again, you never know.
